title: Account Appetite Index and Scope-Swap Protocol
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Top-account escalations currently require manual prioritization conversations that are time-consuming for PMs, SEs, and account teams and often lead to misaligned expectations around scope and delivery windows. We need a repeatable, semi-automated framework that quantifies a customer's appetite for incremental scope, proposes swap candidates (scope de-scopes or staged MVPs), and offers a recommended delivery runway tied to commitment durability metrics.

Goal: Design and pilot an 'Account Appetite Index' (AAI) that scores requests along effort/impact/risk/strategic alignment axes, and pair it with a 'Scope-Swap Protocol' (SSP) that generates two actionable outputs: 1) a scoped MVP + fallback de-scope proposal auto-populated for sales/CS to sign off; 2) an intake-specific recommended runway and credit holdback (commitment durability). Pilot with 4 enterprise accounts during Q1 and measure adoption, time-to-resolution for escalations, and slippage rate on promised deliveries.

Scope:
- Define AAI metric and scoring rubric (numeric).
- Build an intake UI card in Console that auto-populates AAI from form + signals (usage, spend, incident history).
- Create templated SSP output: Primary-Scope (MVP), Swap-Scope (reduced surface), Risk notes, and Runway Recommendation.
- Integrate with PRD template in Drive and generate a short sign-off link for CS.
- Reporting: dashboard to track AAI distribution, average runway, and post-delivery satisfaction.

Out of scope (initial pilot): contractual/legal changes, enforcement of credits, automated billing changes.

Success metrics:
- Pilot adoption: signed SSP for >= 3 of 4 pilot accounts.
- Mean time from escalation intake to committed scope < 7 business days.
- Reduction in scope churn (re-scopes after commitment) by >= 40% vs baseline.
- Positive qualitative feedback from AE/CS and two engineering leads.

Constraints & trade-offs:
- Accuracy of AAI depends on signal quality (we may initially rely on manual inputs).
- Need to avoid adding friction for reps when they file escalations; SSP must be lightweight (<= 10 fields).
- Tension between commercial wants (large feature asks) and engineering capacity; protocol must be advisory with an explicit optional fast-pass escalation path backed by exec review.

Rollout plan:
1) Definition & rubric (2 weeks): agree on axes and weights with GTM, Customer Success, and Eng leads.
2) Mockups & PRD (2 weeks): Console card + sign-off link + reporting spec.
3) Engineering spike (1 week): feasibility for signal ingestion (billing/usage/incidents).
4) Pilot implementation (4 weeks): lightweight Console feature + Drive template + CS workflow.
5) Iterate (3 weeks): gather pilot feedback and tune weights/fields.

Open decisions:
- Numeric weighting of strategic alignment vs engineering effort (proposal: strategic=25%, impact=30%, effort=30%, risk=15%).
- Whether to expose raw AAI to customers or keep it internal. Recommendation: internal only during pilot.
- Default runway buckets (2, 4, 8 weeks) vs continuous days.

Acceptance criteria:
- AAI calculation documented and reproducible from listed signals.
- Console intake card prototype in Figma with <10 fields and prefilled signals.
- SSP auto-generates a Drive PRD draft and a sign-off link that records approver and timestamp.
- Dashboard shows AAI trends and pilot KPIs.
comments: 2025-11-14 — Kickoff: Alignment sync with GTM and Eng. Agreed on initial axes; CS wants 'business impact' separated into revenue and risk-to-renewal. Action: Maya to update rubric draft.

2025-11-20 — PRD draft uploaded: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AaExamplePRD. Feedback from Sarah (CS): prefer a checkbox for 'exec-review-requested' to avoid silent escalations. Added to PRD.
2025-11-27 — Design review: Figma mockups v0.1 shared: https://www.figma.com/file/Example. Design flagged need for compact mobile-friendly view in Console. Estimate reduced fields to 8.

2025-12-03 — Eng spike complete (ENG-1842): signal ingestion feasible via existing billing/usage API; incident history extraction needs a small adapter (ENG-3820). Risk: historical incident data incomplete for two pilot customers.
2025-12-10 — Trade-off discussion: We debated exposing raw AAI to customers. Decided internal-only for pilot to avoid negotiation gaming. Note added to PRD.
2025-12-18 — Pilot cohort identified: Acme Analytics, NovaHealth, FinBridge, Orion Games. CS leads assigned owners. Legal to review sign-off language (non-contractual).
2026-01-05 — Prototype deployed to staging. Console card populates spend and usage signals; manual override allowed. First internal dry-run with AE/CS replicating two previous escalations.

2026-01-14 — Feedback from engineering leads: suggested adding a 'technical risk highlight' auto-populated from recent regressions dashboard (link: https://grafana.example/redwood/regressions). Eng to provide risk mapping by 2026-01-21.

2026-01-20 — Current blocker: Dashboard metrics missing baseline for scope churn. Action: Analytics to backfill 6-month baseline (ENG-3820). Next steps: begin pilot outreach and schedule sign-off demos with two pilot AEs next week.
